cases.name: A01
cases.description: ordinary update: changed + added assets present, the unchanged one omitted entirely

cases.name: A02
cases.description: no current manifest (device on NIL) -> every target asset counts as changed

cases.name: A03
cases.description: every asset unchanged -> changedAssets is an EMPTY object, not null and not absent

cases.name: A04
cases.description: an asset removed in the target simply does not appear; removal is never signalled

cases.name: A05
cases.description: same path, same hash, different position in the manifest -> still unchanged

cases.name: A06
cases.description: hash comparison is case-sensitive: the same hex in upper case counts as CHANGED

cases.name: A07
cases.description: an empty target manifest asset set -> changedAssets is an empty object

cases.name: A08
cases.description: an asset the current manifest holds under a different path counts as changed

cases.name: B01
cases.description: content-addressed: hash is split into sha256/<first two>/<hash><ext>

cases.name: B02
cases.description: content-addressed: the ORIGINAL path is dropped, only the extension survives

cases.name: B03
cases.description: content-addressed: no extension -> no suffix at all

cases.name: B04
cases.description: content-addressed: several dots -> only the LAST segment is the extension

cases.name: B05
cases.description: content-addressed: a dotfile -- "assets/.gitkeep" -- takes ".gitkeep" as its extension

cases.name: B06
cases.description: content-addressed: a trailing dot yields an empty extension after the dot

cases.name: B07
cases.description: content-addressed: a path that already ends in .br keeps .br as the extension

cases.name: B08
cases.description: content-addressed: the base URI's trailing slash is stripped, not doubled

cases.name: B09
cases.description: content-addressed: several trailing slashes are all stripped

cases.name: B10
cases.description: content-addressed: a bucket-root "/assets" base is content-addressed too

cases.name: B11
cases.description: content-addressed: an UPPERCASE hash keeps its case in both the shard and the name

cases.name: B12
cases.description: content-addressed: a hash SHORTER than two characters -- slice(0,2) does not pad or throw

cases.name: B13
cases.description: content-addressed: an EMPTY hash -- the shard segment collapses and is dropped

cases.name: B14
cases.description: content-addressed: a hash of exactly two characters

cases.name: B15
cases.description: content-addressed: a NON-ASCII hash -- slice(0,2) counts UTF-16 units, not bytes

cases.name: B20
cases.description: legacy layout: a base NOT ending in /assets keeps the manifest-relative path verbatim

cases.name: B21
cases.description: legacy layout: a nested path is preserved segment by segment

cases.name: B22
cases.description: legacy layout: a space in the filename is percent-encoded per segment

cases.name: B23
cases.description: legacy layout: "+" is encoded as %2B by encodeURIComponent

cases.name: B24
cases.description: legacy layout: "&" and "=" are encoded

cases.name: B25
cases.description: legacy layout: "#" and "?" are encoded rather than truncating the URI

cases.name: B26
cases.description: legacy layout: non-ASCII is percent-encoded as UTF-8

cases.name: B27
cases.description: legacy layout: an empty path segment (//) is DROPPED, not preserved

cases.name: B28
cases.description: legacy layout: a leading "./" is normalised away by the URL path parser

cases.name: B29
cases.description: legacy layout: a backslash is treated as a SEPARATOR and split on

cases.name: B30
cases.description: legacy layout: a leading slash does not produce a double slash

cases.name: B31
cases.description: legacy layout: a base with NO path at all

cases.name: B32
cases.description: legacy layout: "/assets" as a mid-path segment is NOT content-addressed

cases.name: B33
cases.description: content-addressed: the encoding rules apply to the extension too

cases.name: C01
cases.description: brotli: index.<hash>.bundle at the root matches -> .br suffix and compression

cases.name: C02
cases.description: brotli: index.<hash>.bundle in a subdirectory matches (the (^|/) alternative)

cases.name: C03
cases.description: brotli: a bare "index.bundle" does NOT match -- [^/]+ needs at least one character

cases.name: C04
cases.description: brotli: "index..bundle" does NOT match either

cases.name: C05
cases.description: brotli: several dots between index. and .bundle DO match ([^/]+ spans dots)

cases.name: C06
cases.description: brotli: a filename merely ENDING in index.x.bundle does not match (no separator)

cases.name: C07
cases.description: brotli: the match is anchored at the end -- a trailing .map does not match

cases.name: C08
cases.description: brotli: an ordinary .bundle asset is NOT brotli-compressed

cases.name: C09
cases.description: brotli: a BACKSLASH before index. does not match -- the regex only knows "/"

cases.name: C10
cases.description: brotli under the LEGACY layout: .br is appended to the stored path itself

cases.name: C11
cases.description: brotli: uppercase "Index." does not match -- the regex is case-sensitive

cases.name: D01
cases.description: a patch from the device's current bundle lands on the single .bundle asset

cases.name: D02
cases.description: TWO .bundle assets -> resolveUniqueHbcAssetPath is ambiguous, NO patch is emitted at all

cases.name: D03
cases.description: NO .bundle asset at all -> no patch, the rest of the diff is unaffected

cases.name: D04
cases.description: the unique .bundle asset need not be brotli-shaped: "other.bundle" alone still takes the patch

cases.name: D05
cases.description: the patch names a DIFFERENT base bundle -> getBundlePatch finds nothing, no patch emitted

cases.name: D06
cases.description: baseBundleId matching is CASE-SENSITIVE: an upper-case hex id does not match a lower-case one

cases.name: D06b
cases.description: the same shape with matching case -> the patch IS selected, proving D06 turns on case alone

cases.name: D07
cases.description: device on NIL -> there is no current bundle, so no patch even though one exists

cases.name: D08
cases.description: an EMPTY patchStorageUri is falsy upstream -> the whole descriptor is dropped

cases.name: D09
cases.description: an EMPTY patchFileHash is falsy upstream -> the whole descriptor is dropped

cases.name: D10
cases.description: an EMPTY baseFileHash is falsy upstream -> the whole descriptor is dropped

cases.name: D11
cases.description: two patch records for the SAME base -> the first wins (getBundlePatches dedupes)

cases.name: D12
cases.description: patch records in order [other, matching] -> the matching one is still selected

cases.name: D13
cases.description: the .bundle asset is UNCHANGED -> it is not in changedAssets, so the patch has nowhere to go

cases.name: D14
cases.description: patchStorageUri in ANOTHER bucket -> resolveHbcPatchDescriptor does NOT catch, so the whole check 5xxs
cases.throws: Bucket name mismatch: expected 'bucket', but found 'other-bucket'

cases.name: D15
cases.description: a patch on a ROLLBACK response: artifacts are resolved for rollbacks too

cases.name: E01
cases.description: manifestStorageUri NULL -> no artifacts at all, but the update still ships

cases.name: E02
cases.description: manifestFileHash NULL -> no artifacts (all three columns are required together)

cases.name: E03
cases.description: assetBaseStorageUri NULL -> no artifacts

cases.name: E04
cases.description: an EMPTY manifestFileHash is falsy upstream and drops the artifacts exactly like NULL

cases.name: E05
cases.description: the target manifest object is MISSING -> no artifacts

cases.name: E06
cases.description: the target manifest is not JSON -> no artifacts

cases.name: E07
cases.description: the target manifest is a JSON ARRAY -> isBundleManifest rejects it

cases.name: E08
cases.description: the target manifest has no bundleId -> rejected

cases.name: E09
cases.description: the target manifest bundleId is a NUMBER -> rejected (it must be a string)

cases.name: E10
cases.description: the target manifest has no assets key -> rejected

cases.name: E11
cases.description: an asset whose fileHash is a NUMBER invalidates the WHOLE manifest, not just that asset

cases.name: E12
cases.description: an asset whose SIGNATURE is a number also invalidates the whole manifest

cases.name: E12b
cases.description: a NULL signature is rejected too -- the check is `=== undefined || typeof === "string"`, and null is neither

cases.name: E12c
cases.description: an asset that is an ARRAY is rejected (isBundleManifest excludes arrays per asset)

cases.name: E19
cases.description: assets as an empty ARRAY is ACCEPTED -- Array.isArray is only checked on the manifest and on each asset

cases.name: E20
cases.description: assets as a POPULATED array is accepted too, and the array index becomes the asset path

cases.name: E21
cases.description: an EMPTY manifestStorageUri is falsy and drops the artifacts, exactly like NULL

cases.name: E22
cases.description: an EMPTY assetBaseStorageUri is falsy and drops the artifacts, exactly like NULL

cases.name: E23
cases.description: the CURRENT bundle having an empty manifestStorageUri means no diff base, not a read of ""

cases.name: E13
cases.description: a STRING signature is accepted, and is not carried into the response

cases.name: E14
cases.description: the manifest bundleId need not match the bundle it belongs to -- it is never compared

cases.name: E15
cases.description: the CURRENT manifest is missing -> the update still ships, with every asset marked changed

cases.name: E16
cases.description: the CURRENT manifest is invalid JSON -> same as missing, artifacts still returned

cases.name: E17
cases.description: the current bundle has NO manifestStorageUri -> no diff base, every asset changed

cases.name: E18
cases.description: the device reports an unknown id ABOVE every bundle -> ROLLBACK, and with no diff base every asset is changed

cases.name: F01
cases.description: the ASSET base is in another bucket -> presign throws and, with no patch, the error PROPAGATES
cases.throws: Bucket name mismatch: expected 'bucket', but found 'other-bucket'

cases.name: F02
cases.description: the asset base is in another bucket BUT a patch covers the one .bundle asset: the other assets still throw
cases.throws: Bucket name mismatch: expected 'bucket', but found 'other-bucket'

cases.name: F03
cases.description: a patch covers the ONLY changed asset and its file presign fails -> the asset ships patch-only, no `file` key

cases.name: F04
cases.description: the TARGET MANIFEST is in another bucket -> readText throws and the whole check becomes a 5xx
cases.throws: Bucket name mismatch: expected 'bucket', but found 'other-bucket'

cases.name: F05
cases.description: the CURRENT manifest is in another bucket -> that read throws too, so the check is a 5xx
cases.throws: Bucket name mismatch: expected 'bucket', but found 'other-bucket'

cases.name: F06
cases.description: the BUNDLE itself is in another bucket -> resolveFileUrl throws; fileUrl is never null on an UPDATE
cases.throws: Bucket name mismatch: expected 'bucket', but found 'other-bucket'

cases.name: G01
cases.description: shouldForceUpdate is carried through unchanged on an UPDATE

cases.name: G02
cases.description: a ROLLBACK forces the update regardless of the bundle's own shouldForceUpdate=false

cases.name: G03
cases.description: message and fileHash are carried straight through; storageUri is NOT in the response

cases.name: G04
cases.description: no candidate above the device's bundle and nothing to roll back to -> UP_TO_DATE (null)

cases.name: G05
cases.description: the reset-to-built-in rollback: NIL id, null fileUrl, and NO manifest artifacts are resolved

cases.name: G06
cases.description: a null message stays null rather than being dropped from the response
